screens.name: Landing
screens.title: NeonBoard
screens.purpose: Explain NeonBoard and invite visitors to sign up or sign in to create a dashboard.
screens.composition: Hero band with headline, subcopy about notes, counters, checklists and link lists, and sign-up and sign-in actions over a faint neon grid. Then a strip of four widget-type features with icons, followed by a console-style how-it-works band of create, add widget and autosave. Then a closing call-to-action band inviting the visitor to create a dashboard.

screens.name: Sign up
screens.title: Create account
screens.purpose: Create a new member account and sign in.
screens.composition: Centered narrow card with title, email and password fields and create-account submit, plus a link to sign in. Inline field errors keep typed values, and failure keeps values with retry.

screens.name: Sign in
screens.title: Sign in
screens.purpose: Sign an existing member in to reach dashboards.
screens.composition: Centered narrow card with title, email and password fields and sign-in submit, plus a link to sign up. Inline field errors keep typed values, and failure keeps values with retry.

screens.name: Dashboards
screens.title: Dashboards
screens.purpose: List all of the member's dashboards by last edited and manage them.
screens.composition: Header row with title, dashboard count and Create button. Then cards for the member's dashboards ordered most-recently-edited first, each showing name, last-edited time and duplicate and delete actions. Empty state offers Create as the next action.
screens.frame: Header center shows no dashboard status; sidebar highlights the list and offers Create.

screens.name: Dashboard editor
screens.purpose: Use and edit one dashboard with autosave for all widget changes.
screens.composition: Top area with inline-editable dashboard name, last-edited time and Add widget button. Then the WidgetBoard canvas with faint grid holding WidgetCards in relative order sized small, medium or large. Each card shows its type body with title edit, size, move and remove controls; empty board offers adding a widget.
screens.frame: Header center shows the editable dashboard name with autosaved status; sidebar highlights the current dashboard.

screens.name: Add widget
screens.purpose: Choose the widget type to add to the dashboard.
screens.composition: Dialog with title and description and four large selectable type options for note, counter, checklist and link list. Footer with Cancel and Add actions; a missing type is marked as required.

screens.name: Remove widget
screens.purpose: Confirm permanent removal of one widget.
screens.composition: Small confirm dialog naming the widget and saying its checklist items or links go with it. Footer with Cancel and permanent Remove actions.

screens.name: Delete dashboard
screens.purpose: Confirm permanent deletion of one dashboard and its widgets.
screens.composition: Small confirm dialog naming the dashboard and saying all of its widgets go with it. Footer with Cancel and permanent Delete actions.

newComponents.name: WidgetBoard
newComponents.purpose: Arrange a dashboard's widgets by relative order and small/medium/large size on a glowing grid.
newComponents.whyNotExisting: CardGroup has no size-aware responsive grid or faint neon backdrop, and FlexScrollArea has no ordering and sizing logic for widgets.
newComponents.description: A full-width canvas that holds all WidgetCards in relative order on a dark base with a faint cyan grid behind them. It is low-emphasis background for focus, with soft radius, comfortable density, Inter for helper text and JetBrains Mono for timestamps, and subtle neon edge glow; like the mission-control board of a sci-fi console app.

newComponents.name: WidgetCard
newComponents.purpose: Contain one widget with its title, size and position controls and its type content.
newComponents.whyNotExisting: Card and Section lack inline title editing, small/medium/large variants, move and resize controls, and neon header treatment.
newComponents.description: A bordered tile with a glowing header row holding editable title, move, resize and remove controls, and a type-specific body for note, counter, checklist or link list. It is medium-emphasis on the dark base with cyan/magenta neon border, soft radius, Space Grotesk title, Inter body and JetBrains Mono for counter figures, comfortable density; like an instrument-panel tile in a spaceship dashboard app.

questions.question: Should a counter widget's number have a minimum, maximum, or step other than changing by 1 with no limits?
questions.whyItMatters: Determines whether decrease below zero is allowed and whether stepper needs disabled states or validation.
questions.defaultAnswer: The counter has no minimum or maximum and can be decreased below zero, changing by 1 each time.
